dedupe_keys.name: network centrality and road restoration after the november 2025 flood and landslides in bener meriah aceh

description: This study examines whether the position of damaged roads and bridges in the road network explains how long they took to restore after the flood and landslide event of November 2025 in Bener Meriah Regency, Aceh Province, Indonesia. The dataset behind it records 26 damaged road and bridge assets with road class, construction type, disruption and restoration dates, restoration duration and network centrality measures (degree, betweenness, closeness), the road network graph used to compute them (from OpenStreetMap and institutional road data), and a list of 313 online news articles used to rebuild the disruption and restoration timeline; 3,351 posts on X informed the timeline but are not shared. It was carried out by researchers at the Bandung Institute of Technology, and the manuscript was submitted to Forum Geografi; the data were published on 11 September 2026. Coverage is regional, one regency, at asset level. The three files (a GeoPackage graph and two CSV tables) are free on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. Outcome: the findings are in the submitted manuscript, which was not available to read, so they are not given here. Limitations: the sample is 26 assets and the timeline relies on news reports. The case shows post-event and recovery analysis of a rural road network with digital traces, and complements the FloodNet road flood data catalogued here.
name: Network centrality and road restoration after the November 2025 flood and landslides in Bener Meriah, Aceh
outcomes: Restoration records for 26 assets were linked to network centrality; the findings are reported in a manuscript submitted to Forum Geografi, not yet readable.
provider: Bandung Institute of Technology (Dwi Novi Wulansari and colleagues)
